title: World Bank faults Kenya's Chinese-built railway as graft cases trail Chinese projects from Nepal to Ecuador
dek: Kenya could have saved up to $900 million on the Mombasa-Nairobi line, the World Bank says, with at least 30% of the overspend down to governance failures. Similar cases have followed Chinese-built projects across South Asia and beyond, as Beijing passes a new law on cross-border corruption.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Kenya could have saved up to $900 million on its Chinese-built railway from Mombasa to Nairobi, the World Bank says, and at least 30% of that overspend came from governance failures rather than terrain or engineering. The finding, in the bank's latest Kenya Economic Update, adds Kenya to a growing list of countries where Chinese-financed or Chinese-built projects are tied to corruption cases, from Nepal and Ecuador to Bangladesh.

On Friday, two days after the report was launched in Nairobi, China's top legislature passed a new law against cross-border corruption, reports said. Beijing presents it as proof that it polices its companies abroad. Critics point to how rarely such cases have reached a Chinese court.

## What the World Bank found in Kenya

The Standard Gauge Railway was built by China Road and Bridge Corporation between 2014 and 2017, largely with loans from the Export-Import Bank of China. The World Bank report, published on 3 November, says the Mombasa-Nairobi line cost $7.6 million per kilometre, against $5.7 million for Tanzania's Dar es Salaam-Dodoma line and $5.3 million for the Djibouti-Addis Ababa line, both of which are electrified ([World Bank, Kenya Economic Update No. 34](https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099110226121518967/pdf/P518942-68dd8254-9e64-46ca-b177-6d46a9861e0f.pdf)).

> "With the same cost metric as the Tanzanian line, Kenya could have saved up to US$900 million in initial construction costs. Of this amount, at least 30 percent is considered attributable to governance challenges."

The bank lists those challenges as "the preference for direct contracting rather than competitive tendering; land speculation; and outright fraud around titling, valuation, and compensation payments". It notes that each line has its own cost drivers and that land in Kenya is more expensive, but says that does not fully explain the gap.

The report goes beyond the railway. It calls corruption "the key binding constraint" on Kenya's growth, estimates that weak governance widens the budget deficit by about 2% of GDP a year, and finds that 36% of firms faced at least one bribe request in the past year. Treasury Principal Secretary Chris Kiptoo responded that "good governance is not separate to our development agenda -- it is the foundation", one report said. The Declaration found no response from China's embassy or the contractor.

The railway's legal record is mixed. Kenya's Court of Appeal ruled in 2020 that the procurement broke the law, but the Supreme Court overturned that in June 2023 and held it was lawful ([Kenya Law](https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/judgment/kesc/2023/38/eng@2023-06-16)). Separately, Weihai Construction Group, which the African Development Bank barred for 35 months in 2021 for "fraudulent practices" on Kenyan road and water projects, has won a Sh3.2 billion road contract in Busia County, Kenyan media reported this week ([AfDB](https://allafrica.com/stories/202112230490.html)).

## The cases elsewhere

- **Nepal:** In December 2025 the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority charged China CAMC Engineering and 55 people, including five former ministers, over Pokhara International Airport, built with a $216 million China Exim Bank loan. It alleges a loss of Rs 8.36 billion through inflated costs. A second case in May charged a former finance minister and CAMC's chairman over a tax waiver. China's ambassador told Nepal's prime minister that CAMC, as a state-owned company, could not be involved in corruption under Chinese law, one report said. The case is before the Special Court.
- **Ecuador:** On 28 August Ecuador's National Court of Justice convicted former president Lenín Moreno of bribery over the Sinohydro-built Coca Codo Sinclair dam and sentenced him to five years. A former Chinese ambassador, Cai Runguo, and two former Sinohydro representatives were also convicted, one report said. Prosecutors say about $76 million in bribes was paid between 2009 and 2018. Moreno says he "has not received a single cent from Sinohydro" and is appealing.
- **Bangladesh:** In 2018 Dhaka blacklisted China Harbour Engineering Company after then finance minister AMA Muhith said it offered Tk 5 million to a senior roads official, and cancelled the company's Dhaka-Sylhet highway deal.
- **Sri Lanka:** One report said in 2018 that $7.6 million from an account controlled by China Harbour went to affiliates of Mahinda Rajapaksa's 2015 campaign. China Harbour called the report "distorted and false" and Rajapaksa denied it. No outcome of an investigation has been published.
- **Malaysia:** At former prime minister Najib Razak's 1MDB trial in 2019, a former aide testified that the Chinese-built East Coast Rail Link and two pipeline projects were meant to help bail out 1MDB; the contractor denied it. Malaysia renegotiated the rail link in 2019, cutting its cost from RM65.5 billion to RM44 billion.
- **World Bank blacklists:** In May the World Bank barred state-owned China National Technical Import & Export Corporation for 18 months over energy projects in Pakistan, Bangladesh and the Maldives, saying it failed to disclose commissions paid to third parties. The company acknowledged responsibility ([World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2026/05/27/world-bank-group-debars-china-national-technical-import-export-corporation)). From 2009 to 2017 the bank barred China Communications Construction Company and its subsidiaries for fraud on a Philippine roads project ([World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2011/07/29/world-bank-applies-2009-debarment-to-china-communications-construction-company-limited-for-fraud-in-philippines-roads-project)).

The cases in Nepal and Ecuador were brought by those countries' own institutions and named local politicians alongside Chinese companies and officials.

## Beijing's answer

China made bribing foreign officials a crime in 2011, but analysts have found few, if any, publicised prosecutions under that provision. The new law, 47 articles long, was passed by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on 6 November. The draft covered bribery of foreign officials by Chinese citizens and companies, required firms working abroad to run compliance systems, and barred foreign agencies from carrying out enforcement in China without approval ([Arnold & Porter](https://www.arnoldporter.com/en/perspectives/advisories/2026/09/china-issues-draft-anti-cross-border-corruption-law)). The final text has not yet been published in English. Beijing has long promised a "clean Silk Road" for its Belt and Road projects.

## What it means for India and Bengal

Three of China's closest South Asian partners, Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, appear in these cases. This week China's party envoy Liu Haixing told a roundtable in Dhaka that work on two Chinese-backed projects, the Teesta river plan and an industrial park at Mongla port, is "advancing steadily" ([The Declaration](https://thedeclaration.in/story/china-liu-haixing-dhaka-tarique-teesta-mongla-bnp/)). The Teesta flows into Bangladesh from north Bengal, and Mongla lies on the Bay of Bengal. How Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's new government tenders and audits these deals will be watched closely in New Delhi and Kolkata. The World Bank's ban on a Chinese state firm in May already covered energy projects in Bangladesh.

## What to watch

- **Kenya:** whether parliament or the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission acts on the World Bank's railway finding.
- **Nepal:** hearings in the Pokhara airport case at the Special Court.
- **Ecuador:** Moreno's appeal against his conviction.
- **China:** publication of the full text of the cross-border corruption law, and whether any Chinese company is prosecuted under it.
